slide_text: Visualizing Data using t-SNE
Laurens van der Maaten¹, Geoffrey Hinton²¹TiCC, Tilburg University, Tilburg, The Netherlands. ²Department of Computer Science, University of Toronto, Toronto, Canada.
Introduction

• Dimensionality reduction maps each observation to a point in 2D or 3D.
• Point arrangements reveal which relationships the map preserves.
• Single-variable displays can obscure relationships across multiple dimensions.
• Images and documents can have many variables per observation, and datasets can contain thousands of observations.
Stochastic Neighbor Embedding

• SNE converts input distances into conditional neighbor probabilities.
• Gaussian kernels assign higher probabilities to closer neighbors.
◦ One bandwidth per input observation
• Low-dimensional maps define corresponding conditional neighbor distributions.
• SNE minimizes summed Kullback–Leibler divergence from input to map distributions.
t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding
Symmetric SNE

• Symmetric SNE expresses pairwise similarities as joint probabilities.
◦ Averages two directional conditional probabilities per pair.
The Crowding Problem

• 2D maps crowd points when preserving neighborhood distances.
• High-dimensional manifolds can accommodate many neighbors at moderate distances.
• A uniform background opens cluster gaps. Direct optimization barely attracts similar points separated early.
Mismatched Tails can Compensate for Mismatched Dimensiona…

• t-SNE defines map similarities using a Student t-distribution.
◦ One degree of freedom
• Heavy tails map moderate input distances farther apart, reducing crowding.
Optimization Methods for t-SNE

• Early exaggeration amplifies input similarities 4× for the first 50 iterations.
◦ 1,000 total iterations
• Early compression and early exaggeration help clusters rearrange during fitting.
Experiments
Data Sets

• MNIST has 6,000 handwritten digit images.
• Olivetti supplies 400 face images of 40 people to compare identity grouping.
◦ 40 people
Experimental Setup
• Reduce inputs to 30 principal components before fitting 2D maps.
Results
• t-SNE nearly separates MNIST digit classes.

• The t-SNE map preserves variation among handwritten examples of the same digit.
◦ Differences in stroke orientation within digit classes
• t-SNE better separates many COIL-20 object manifolds. Similar cars can remain close.
Applying t-SNE to Large Data Sets

• Landmark t-SNE maps 6,000 MNIST digits using all 60,000 images.
◦ Visible variation within digit classes
• The 2D map lowers 1-nearest-neighbor error from 5.75% to 5.13%.
◦ Tenfold cross-validation against original pixel space
• Random walks on the full neighborhood graph estimate landmark affinities.
Discussion
Comparison with Related Techniques

• Scaling methods balance local relationships and large-scale structure differently.
◦ Classical scaling, Sammon mapping, and neighborhood-based methods
• Weights on errors at small distances shape which relationships dominate.
Weaknesses

• t-SNE performance beyond three target dimensions remains uncertain.
• Lighter-tailed similarities may better preserve local structure in higher-dimensional maps.
• High intrinsic dimensionality can weaken input neighborhood information.
• Nonconvex optimization offers no guarantee of finding a global optimum.
Conclusions

• t-SNE preserves fine-scale relationships and reveals clusters at multiple scales.
• Landmark mapping uses full-dataset random walks to visualize larger datasets.
• Proposed extensions tune Student t degrees of freedom.
◦ Multiple map points per input observation
◦ Learned mapping for previously unseen observations
